newsitem.title: USA: US EIA hikes Q1 oil price forecast to $23.18/bbl.
newsitem.headline: US EIA hikes Q1 oil price forecast to $23.18/bbl.

text.p: U.S. oil prices, including imports, should average $23.18 per barrel in the first quarter of 1997, the Energy Information Administration said Wednesday, hiking its previous forecast for the quarter by $1.38.
With the higher outlook for the first quarter, the U.S. agency raised its outlook for 1997 to an average of $21.50, up from a previous forecast of $21.04, and up from last year's average of $20.57.
The agency still expected prices to fall by about $1.00 between the first and second quarters.

"Strong world oil demand and relatively low inventories have kept persistent pressure on spot prices in recent months," EIA said in material prepared at an Independent Petroleum Association of America conference in New Orleans and released in Washington.
Total U.S. crude oil stocks stand at 292 million barrels, about 4 percent lower than a year ago.

EIA said it saw natural gas wellhead prices in 1997 holding at the same level as 1996 at $2.17 per thousand cubic feet, up from a previous forecast of $2.09, based on the assumption that winter weather would be normal.

"Very cold weather could still rapidly deplete gas in storage, push spot prices up again and put pressure on the wellhead market that could last well into the summer," it said. "This seems to be less of a threat now, as we head into February with storage moving toward and above year-ago levels."
While gasoline inventories do not normally draw attention during the winter, EIA said "low gasoline stocks have become a source of concern."
Gasoline stocks at the end of last week stood at 207 million barrels, down from 213.5 million barrels a year ago.
But it said that because stocks of distillate -- heating oil and diesel -- were low, refiners were keeping their plants running at full steam at a time when they would normally slow down runs.

The higher output should help to beef up gasoline stocks. "If refinery runs remain high during the winter for distillate production, this (gasoline stock) situation could improve significantly before spring," EIA said.
